Australia's Toyota Hilux Posts New October Sales Record, Sells 42,570 Units YTD
12 photos
Photo: Toyota
Last month, Toyota dealers moved no fewer than 5,954 units of the Hilux in Australia, setting a new record for the month. That sales volume also secured the Hilux's eighth-highest monthly result ever, going to show that consumer demand for the new-gen model is healthy.
Better still for Toyota and the Hilux , which is a different animal from the North American-market Tacoma, the mid-size pickup has reclaimed first place in year-to-date terms. The Hilux finally managed to beat the Ford Motor Company's Ranger, with Toyota moving 1,113 more units.
The October 2026 tally represents a 34 percent increase over the 4,444 units delivered in October 2026, marking the first time the Hilux topped the monthly sales chart in 2026. Last year, it claimed the number one position five times. Indeed, the Hilux is one of the best-selling vehicles in the Land Down Under.
Looking at the bigger picture, Toyota's RAV4 claimed third place in October 2026 with 4,718 sales to its name. Introduced a year ago in Australia, Thailand, and Europe simultaneously, the ninth generation of the Hilux is the first one developed from the outset to support BEV and FCEV powertrains.
The Australian rollout took a bit longer to reach its full potential, with certain important configurations arriving at dealers in the latter part of 2026. Prospective customers, therefore, had fewer options during the first months of the ninth gen. Vehicle availability needs mentioning as well, with stock leaving much to be desired through early fall.
Photo: Toyota In any case, I would be careful about interpreting a record month as proof that the ninth-generation Hilux is a commercial success. A model that spent months waiting for allocation is capable of producing an exceedingly healthier monthly result once supply catches up, and the broader year-to-date figures reveal a far less flattering picture.
Between January 2026 and October 2026, the Hilux delivered 42,570 units in the Australian market. That's 129 vehicles behind the Ford Ranger, and the Tesla Model Y is right behind it with 39,035 deliveries through October 2025. The RAV4 is listed fourth with 35,927 sales, while China's BYD Sealion 7 has clocked 22,488 deliveries in the analyzed ten-month timeframe.
Per the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries, legacy automakers like Toyota and Ford are facing increasingly more competition from Chinese newcomers. China served as the largest source of vehicles recorded through VFACTS in October 2026, supplying 36.3 percent of everything delivered last month. Japan followed with 23.3 percent, then Thailand with 17.9 percent.
In terms of brands, Toyota led monthly sales with 20,649 vehicles compared to 10,025 for second-placed BYD and 7,310 for Ford. Kia and Mazda delivered 5,801 and 5,730 vehicles, respectively, while MG slots above Hyundai in this regard. Just below the South Korean automaker, Great Wall Motor delivered 4,417 vehicles compared to 4,365 for Geely and 4,317 for Chery.
